messages:
katie: FYI: multiple customers reporting 504/gateway timeouts on hosted inference around 10:12 UTC. Looks correlated with a tenant surge to a few pools. I can repro via stress tests.
eng-oncall: Can you paste the gateway logs and any recent autoscaler events? Suspect HPA/KEDA interaction or readiness probe delays.
katie: Copying snippets: 
```
[2026-03-17T10:12:14Z] gateway: upstream error: 504 FastCGI timeout (scaleup queued)
[2026-03-17T10:12:16Z] provisioner: enqueue tenant=acme-prod requested_replicas=8 current=1
[2026-03-17T10:12:45Z] readiness: pod/x-12 init: model-fetch (download 0%)
```
Also seeing a backlog metric on scaledObject: queueLength spiking to 190.
sre-bot: alert: tenant-surge-high-queue fired (p95 latency > 6s)
jordan: What are the KEDA ScaledObject settings? pollingInterval / cooldownPeriod? If pollingInterval is high the scaler reacts slowly.
katie: scaledObject snippet: 
```
triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://metrics:9090
      metricName: tenant_queue_length
      threshold: "50"
pollingInterval: "30"
cooldownPeriod: "300"
minReplicaCount: "1"
maxReplicaCount: "12"
```
tom: That pollingInterval of 30s + cooldown 300s is pretty conservative. During a sudden surge KEDA won't scale up fast enough and HPA feels starved. Also readiness probe for model init is quite long (20s) so warmup adds latency.
support-lead: Customer impact: 3 paid accounts reported API 5xx and 1 escalated to CSM. We should triage and provide mitigation steps ASAP.
jordan: Quick mitigation options: 
- temporarily bump minReplicaCount to 3 for high-traffic tenants (reduces cold starts)
- lower pollingInterval to 5s and cooldown to 120s for the scaledObject 
- add a short-lived prewarm job that pulls model cache before traffic arrives
I can open a config change if eng-oncall approves.
eng-oncall: Agree. For immediate relief, set minReplicaCount=3 and reduce pollingInterval. Also enable a short prober that warms the KV cache: `curl /internal/warm?model=redwood-7b`.
katie: Ran `kubectl patch scaledobject tenant-acme -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":"3"}}'` and lowered polling to 5s in test cluster. Observed queue drop from 190 -> 22 in ~60s, 504s falling.
prod-deploy-bot: deploy: rollout/patch scaledobject/tenant-acme scheduled by eng-oncall
support-lead: Noted—I'll update customers and keep the status page message drafted.
tom: Longer-term fixes: better burst prewarming, reduce heavy model downloads at pod start (stream model shard load), and add autoscaler signal aggregation so KEDA + HPA don't fight. Also consider making readiness return fast while background-loading weights with a soft-serving path.
jordan: Also check auth/billing path: some 502s were auth-related earlier. Confirmed billing-service had a short token refresh failure at 10:11:58 but that recovered; not the main cause of 504s but compounded retries. Patch to rotate tokens more gracefully is queued.
katie: Repro steps I used for the postmortem: 
1) run `ab` style load against /v1/generate with 50 concurrent clients for 90s hitting tenant header X-Tenant: acme-prod 
2) observe scaledObject metric `tenant_queue_length` and gateway 504s
3) watch pod readiness logs for model-fetch stalls
Commands: 
```
ab -n 10000 -c 50 -H "X-Tenant: acme-prod" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
kubectl get hpa,scaledobject -o wide --namespace inference
kubectl logs -l tenant=acme-prod -c runtime
```
eng-oncall: Next actions (short): patch minReplicaCount and pollingInterval for the affected tenant pools; enable warm probe; post status. Mid-term: design change to prewarm strategy + decrease model init latency.
support-lead: I'll close the customer escalations loop once we confirm no recurrence in next 2 hours.
sre-bot: alert: tenant-surge-high-queue resolved
tom: leaving notes for postmortem: label this as autoscaler latency + heavy model warmup. Possible contributing factors: aggressive cooldown, large model shard downloads, auth token rotation spike.
katie: saving logs and will draft the incident writeup. Thanks all :thumbsup:
